[1/6] Plan: add a literature-based e-consent flow and a privacy-preserving email data-return path for future research articles

impact_assessment.why: The user wants Noesis to collect data for future articles; that requires documented informed consent, a pseudonymous participant code, and a user-triggered way to send the export to the study team's email without adding a server or silent data transmission
impact_assessment.benefits: Opt-in research participation; bilingual EN/TR consent; versioned consent record in the export; email draft + JSON download; no account, no server, no automatic send
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new storage keys, a new consent screen, export schema fields and Settings panel; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: existing local data remains valid, new optional fields
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first storage/UI/export tests, pure email-draft builder, no network code, browser proof of consent + download, full gates

[1/5] Plan: log every session start, completion and early ending so adherence and dropout are measurable in research exports

impact_assessment.why: The review makes adherence a primary metric (R22) and the export currently contains only completed sessions; dropout cannot be measured, which blocks the app as a data collector for future articles. A pilot RCT in computerized training reported 38.5%/57.1% dropout (PMID 30881315), so starts and early endings must be logged.
impact_assessment.benefits: Session-level adherence log with seed, timestamps, blocks completed and arm; export and Settings summary; no server and no change to cognitive scores
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new storage key, export field and Settings prop; dependency: none; concurrency: no cross-tab guarantees beyond existing local storage; state: old exports remain valid because adherence defaults to []
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first storage/export/UI tests, explicit start/complete/abort paths, dangling-start closure on a new session, full gates and browser proof

[1/5] Plan: add analysis-ready CSV exports for session blocks and adherence events, grounded in FAIR/data-reuse guidance

impact_assessment.why: The JSON export is complete but not directly analysis-ready in R/SPSS; researchers must flatten nested results and adherence events by hand, which invites transcription errors and weakens reuse. FAIR data guidance calls for interoperable, reusable formats and metadata.
impact_assessment.benefits: Stable CSV headers, one row per block/event, escaped cells, complete metrics JSON, local download; no server or PII change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new export builders and Settings buttons; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no storage change
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first CSV/UI tests, a browser download proof, FAIR note and full gates
